artifacts.summary: 9-phase, 5-wave plan to delete dispatch-worktree.sh and its two test suites and unwire all 13 surviving reference files, including the dual-purpose predicate rename, two correctness fixes, four test suites the dispatch never named, the repo-root .gitignore, and honest post-removal re-measurement of both byte-budget gates.

memory_candidates.content: Before deleting a test group as part of a feature teardown, check whether it stages shared fixtures (stubs, log files, sandbox scripts) that LATER groups in the same suite consume. Test suites commonly let one group write stubs into a sandbox and have subsequent groups document that they 'reuse' those still-live stubs rather than re-staging them. Here a group being deleted staged three stubs; only one belonged to the removed feature, and two later groups depended on the other two, so a wholesale group deletion would have broken surviving coverage with a confusing exec-not-found failure far from the edit. The fix is to extract the non-feature stub staging into a retained, clearly-labelled shared setup block (renaming any group-prefixed variable) and run the suite after the extraction but BEFORE the deletion, so the dependency is proven handled rather than assumed.
